rigorrun.implementation: repository sources at this commit run with pnpm rigorrun (tsx); the 0.2.0 tarball in dist/ carries the same version and was not re-packed

email-mcp.environment: local MailHog container (documented by upstream) as the primary sink; local GreenMail fake IMAP/SMTP container behind a loopback STARTTLS relay as a labelled supplement
limitations: MailHog has no IMAP, so folder/move/delete/flag tools cannot be exercised against it (they need an IMAP backend)
the auto-responder and watcher modules are absent from the repository, so those 13 tools cannot run at all (finding E-2)
the GreenMail track is a deviation from the MailHog-only instruction and is reported separately

worktide-mcp.environment: self-authored docker compose from upstream docs/INSTALL-docker-compose.md: FrankenPHP dev image, MySQL 8.0, Valkey; fixtures loaded; personal access token minted through the REST API; no ddev

upstream_tests.command: (none: the repository has no test suite; package.json's test:tools points at a file that does not exist)

limitations: the two SPAs were not built (not needed: the REST API and MySQL are the oracle)
the backend's own PHPUnit suite was not run (the target under audit is the MCP server; the backend is the fixture)
MCP commit (2026-07-10) predates the backend commit (2026-08-01); findings are stated against exactly these two commits

sqlite-mcp.runtime: Rust 2024 edition, built with cargo 1.98.1 inside rust:1-bookworm
sqlite-mcp.environment: a disposable SQLite file created from scripts/seed-sqlite.sql for every case
limitations: no `rigorrun verify` run: the sandbox only builds Node servers from npm: or dir: references
RigorRun has no independent-oracle assertion type; its verdicts rest on the target server's own nominated reads, so the audit's ground truth had to live outside RigorRun
RigorRun has no headless project setup; the runner's HTTP API was driven directly (the same routes the interface calls)
RigorRun's generated cases carry a fixed 15 s budget; the 8B local model and the 47-tool email catalogue did not fit inside it
one machine, one day, three servers: nothing here generalises to the MCP server population
